nodes.title: AXD301 'nine nines' is an undocumented slide, not a measurement
nodes.summary: Armstrong's own 2003 thesis says the only long-term stability evidence for AXD301 was a PowerPoint claiming a major customer ran an 11-node system at 99.9999999%, with collection method undocumented. Design target was 5 nines ('better than 5 nines'); Ericsson engineer says Erlang cannot take all credit (duplicated hardware, ATM switch design).
nodes.specifics: Thesis s8.5; AXD301 snapshot 1.13M LOC Erlang, 141 apps in supervision tree, 92% of functions side-effect-free, <4 dirty fns/kLOC (thesis s8.2-8.3). erlang-questions 2008-06-12 (Ulf Wiger): approved external quote only from British Telecom. DESIGN IMPLICATION (falsifiable): AEGIS must not cite 'let-it-crash gives N nines' as evidence; availability claims must come from its own DST/chaos harness with logged downtime; acceptance gate = measured request-success SLO under injected handler faults over >=1e6 requests with published logs.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Treating the thesis as proof the architecture is bad: AXD301 was real, large (1.1M LOC) and long-lived; the claim is just unmeasured.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Dismissing supervision trees: the 141-app tree and clean/dirty function split are real structural evidence of isolation discipline.

nodes.title: Let-it-crash fails when the crash domain is a shared VM resource (Cowboy/Cowlib CVEs 2026)
nodes.summary: Supervision restarts a process but cannot protect shared BEAM resources: plug_cowboy HTTP/2 :scheme -> String.to_atom exhausts the atom table and kills the whole VM; Cowlib HPACK/QPACK unbounded integer decode exhausts memory node-wide; Cowboy multipart read_part unbounded (<2.15.0).
nodes.specifics: CVE-2026-32688 / GHSA-q8x4-x7mp-5vg2: plug_cowboy 2.0.0-2.8.0, fixed 2.8.1, published 2026-04-27, CVSS4 8.7, CWE-770, workaround disable HTTP/2. CVE-2026-59248: cowlib >=2.0.0 <2.19.0 unbounded HPACK/QPACK prefixed int (cow_hpack_common:dec_big_int/3), confirmed via api.osv.dev (NVD page not fetchable). DESIGN IMPLICATION: every per-request resource (interned strings, header tables, integer width) needs a per-connection budget enforced BEFORE allocation; isolation unit must own its memory (per-handler arena/instance), not share a global table. Test: fuzz harness feeding unique :scheme/header values and 10^6-octet varints asserts RSS growth < fixed bound and process survives.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Generalising from 3 Elixir/Erlang-library CVEs to 'BEAM is unsafe'; Cowboy itself is ISC, 7.5k stars, actively maintained.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Missing that the same class (unbounded allocation in parsers) recurs in Rust stacks too (h2, quinn); it is language-agnostic.

nodes.title: PHP's crash immunity is process-level recycling plus watchdogs, not a language property; no public crash-isolation measurements exist
nodes.summary: Share-nothing = every request rebuilds state, shared data pushed to DB/cache tier (Lerdorf: 'scale horizontally infinitely'). FPM implements robustness operationally: pm.max_requests (respawn to work around leaks in 3rd-party libs), request_terminate_timeout (kill worker), emergency_restart_threshold (restart FPM if N children SIGSEGV/SIGBUS in interval), all default OFF. PHP internals 2020 thread: isolation seen as robustness feature; Swoole/RoadRunner give up isolation for speed. I found no quantified public data on crash blast radius or per-request bootstrap cost.
nodes.specifics: php.net FPM config manual; externals.io/message/108253 (2020); tideways blog; talks.php.net share-nothing slides. DESIGN IMPLICATION: define 'PHP miracle' as four testable invariants: (I1) handler fault (panic/abort/OOM/infinite loop) affects only that request, (I2) no cross-request memory residue, (I3) per-request CPU/mem/time hard cap, (I4) crash-loop damping (threshold analog of emergency_restart). Acceptance gate: chaos test injecting each fault class at 5% of requests while 95% concurrent healthy requests keep p99 within 1.2x baseline.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Claiming PHP is 'crash-immune': a SEGV in a shared extension kills the worker and its in-flight request; FPM needs a threshold knob because it can crash-loop.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Ignoring that real hosting (WordPress, Facebook-era) ran at huge scale on this model; density came from simplicity, not proofs.

nodes.title: CGI->FastCGI->AOLserver: the cost of isolation was per-request state setup; the fix was pooling OUTSIDE the isolation boundary
nodes.summary: FastCGI (Open Market, spec v1.0 1996-04-29, Mark R. Brown) removed per-request process creation by persistent processes. AOLserver (NaviSoft->AOL 1995, open-sourced 1999) combined multithreading, embedded Tcl and pooled persistent DB connections (~100x vs CGI per Wikipedia only), at the price of in-process shared fate; NaviServer fork 2005 still active. Pattern: isolation cheap if expensive state (DB conns, compiled code) lives in a trusted pool and handlers receive references.
nodes.specifics: FastCGI spec/whitepaper (whitepaper URL 404 on Apple mirror; spec at mit.edu mirror). DESIGN IMPLICATION: connection pools, TLS sessions, prepared-statement caches live in a broker; handlers get capability handles; falsifiable bench: per-request instantiate+DB-handle-acquire overhead < 100us p50 at >=10k rps on one core, else isolation boundary is mis-placed.
nodes.overclaim_risk: 100x figure is a single Wikipedia sentence.
nodes.underclaim_risk: AOLserver's architecture (threads+pools+script) became the template for most app servers.

nodes.title: Ur/Web statically rules out injection and gives automatic CSRF signing, but explicitly does NOT guarantee authorization correctness
nodes.summary: Per the manual's Security Model (FFI unused, checkable from .urp): no SQLi/XSS (code is AST, not strings), automatic CSRF via signed cookies when a handler reads cookies and has side effects, locked-down stdlib (no filesystem). Explicit non-guarantees: any endpoint can be called with any args/cookies; CSRF signature not handler-specific; FFI voids warranty. POPL'15 (not PLDI): compiler SML ~55,000 LOC, server runtime ~5,000 LOC C, client ~1,500 LOC JS.
nodes.specifics: Chlipala POPL'15 DOI 10.1145/2676726.2677004; urweb doc/manual.tex 'Security Model'. DESIGN IMPLICATION: type-level removal of injection classes is a solved, cheap result (typed SQL + typed HTML AST); AEGIS must get it in its handler SDK (parameterized-query-only DB API, HTML as AST) and must add an authz layer Ur/Web lacks; invariant test: no API path exists that accepts a raw SQL/HTML string without a named unsafe_ escape hatch, enforced by grep-able lint + cargo-geiger-style budget.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Saying Ur/Web 'prevents CSRF' without the cookie/signature caveat.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Underrating: BazQux/Bitparking ran years with no reported classic web vulns (self-reported by developer, grade C).

nodes.title: Ur/Web stayed niche: bus factor 1, no release since 2020-02-09, TechEmpower strength unrevalidatable
nodes.summary: Best-in-class result existed (TFB Round 9: 4th throughput ~110k req/s, best latency 2.1ms on fortunes at 40 threads, but poor on many-write test due to transaction analysis/restart) yet repo shows 37 contributors, achlipala 2415 of 2801 commits (86%), last tagged release 20200209, no commits since 2024-06, 851 stars; BazQux repo 87 stars last push 2021-06. Developers' top pain: whole-program client/server sidedness analysis gives confusing errors; metaprogramming (dependent-type-like) barely used in production apps. TechEmpower sunset 2026-03-24.
nodes.specifics: gh api urweb/urweb (2026-10-24); POPL'15 s4.1-4.2 (12 external patch contributors, BazQux 2500 paying users, 10 rps avg, >150 peak). DESIGN IMPLICATION: do not make a niche-language handler SDK the only path; falsifiable: any language/toolchain dependency with <5 active maintainers or no release in 24 months is a go/no-go blocker unless vendored with a reproducible build and an exit plan.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Using star/commit counts as quality; it is a maintenance-risk signal only.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Coding agents do not obviously fix a maintainer-count blocker; LLM competence on Ur/Web is unmeasured (assume low from corpus size).

nodes.title: Hails (OSDI'12): IFC web framework with measured 1.7x throughput loss vs Jetty and poor policy-API ergonomics; repos dormant since 2016
nodes.summary: Haskell/LIO, model policies (trusted) vs view-controllers (untrusted). httperf, 100 closed-loop conns, 2x Xeon E5620, GbE: Pong 47,577 r/s vs Jetty 82,275 (1.7x fewer), +28% vs Apache+PHP, 47x Sinatra; Table 30%/23% below Jetty/PHP, 6x Sinatra; no response pipelining blamed. Experience: 4 developers; policy implementation API 'difficult to learn'; one blog app leaked unpublished posts via policy bug; mass-assignment bugs became non-vulnerabilities thanks to policy; privilege delegation largely avoided.
nodes.specifics: scslab/hails 52 stars last push 2016-09; scslab/lio 3 stars 2016-07. DESIGN IMPLICATION: security policy must be a small declarative artifact owned by trusted code, with analysis (SMT) over policies; test: policy-DSL conformance suite where an agent-written handler with deliberately wrong code cannot read rows outside policy (differential: same handler with/without policy returns different rows only where policy denies).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Hardware is 2012; do not quote 1.7x as current.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Hails numbers (PHP comparable) show IFC overhead was not what killed it.

nodes.title: LWeb (POPL'19) and Storm (OSDI'21) fixed Hails' blockers: 2-21% overhead, then zero runtime cost, TCB <1% of app code
nodes.summary: LWeb: LIO+Yesod, noninterference mechanized in Liquid Haskell, 2-21% runtime overhead vs manual checks, BIBIFI site with 40 tables, TCB ~1% of app (21% incl. LWeb). Storm: refinement-typed security ORM over LIO, trusted code <1%, no runtime cost, 1 type annotation per 19 LOC (1/29 non-trivial), verification seconds per controller on i7-8550U laptop, 9 ported policy case studies, deployed Disco (107 users, peak 55, 2020). Limitation: controllers confined to restricted RIO monad; exceptions hard.
nodes.specifics: Both Haskell/Liquid Haskell, research-grade, no production adoption found. DESIGN IMPLICATION: statically-checked authz/IFC on DB access is feasible at ~5% annotation tax; the annotation tax is exactly what coding agents are good at; falsifiable pilot: have an agent write 10 handlers against a Rust refinement/typestate DB-gate API; success = >=90% compile+pass policy tests within 5 iterations, and 0 policy-violating handlers compile.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Storm 'no run-time cost' is relative to the unchecked LIO baseline on case studies, not a system benchmark.
nodes.underclaim_risk: These papers show perf was never the real blocker; ecosystem and language choice were.

nodes.title: Swift/Jif (SOSP'07): automatic client/server partitioning by IFC labels worked on 6 small apps; died on cost of a new language stack
nodes.summary: Swift compiler adds ~20,000 LOC to Jif/Polyglot; runtime ~2,600 LOC Java; WebIL UI framework 1,400 lines; 6 apps, largest Shop 1094 Jif lines -> 1.21 MB JS (null program 73 kB), claim of performance comparable to hand-written (no hard numbers in fetched copy). Jif itself: documented limits include timing channels and omitted features; 3.3.1 latest docs seen. Lasting idea: security-critical code/data pinned to the server by label, replicated checks on the client for UX only.
nodes.specifics: Paper fetched (6-page version). DESIGN IMPLICATION: retain 'client checks are advisory, server re-checks are authoritative' as a mechanical invariant: every validation expressed once in a shared schema and the server always re-validates; test: mutation test deleting any client-side check must not change server acceptance set.
nodes.overclaim_risk: No adoption data located; 'died' inferred from absence.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Underrates conceptual influence on Hails/LWeb/Storm lineage.

nodes.title: Joe-E/Waterken: capability-safe Java subset worked (13K SLOC Joe-E + 4K Java server), but library taming was the admitted weakest link
nodes.summary: Joe-E verifier (Eclipse plugin) statically checks capability discipline; Waterken server uses it to prove persistence consistency (Immutable-marked Transaction/return types prevent vat escape). Authors call taming the Java stdlib 'time-consuming and difficult... a substantial weakness'; DarpaBrowser review found taming mistakes in E's database. Requires capability-training for developers. Repo davidwagner/joe-e 4 stars, last push 2015-06.
nodes.specifics: NDSS 2010 (Mettler, Wagner, Close); Mettler thesis EECS-2012-244. DESIGN IMPLICATION (Rust analog): the stdlib is the taming problem. Enforce no-ambient-authority by (a) deny std::fs/net/process/env via clippy disallowed-methods + a workspace lint, (b) route all effects through cap-std style Dir/Pool handles, where code must call ambient_authority() explicitly (cap-std docs note it is not a sandbox against unsafe). CI gate: cargo-deny/grep fails build if any handler crate references std::{fs,net,process,env} or declares unsafe.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Waterken's persistence property is about one server, not a deployed ecosystem.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Rust's ownership gives much of Joe-E's 'no static mutable state' for free; the residual is unsafe + stdlib ambient APIs.

nodes.title: Web-key/YURL capability URLs: the bearer-URL design leaks (Referer, http, third-party scripts); W3C TAG could only issue non-normative good practices
nodes.summary: Tyler Close's httpsy://, YURLs and web-key put authority in the URL (hash of root key inside, so key replacement keeps URLs valid). W3C TAG 'Good Practices for Capability URLs' (Tennison, non-normative Finding, 2014) was motivated by leaked doc-sharing URLs and lists leak routes; Referrer-Policy helps but 'is not enough'. TAG did not dispute but never endorsed web-key.
nodes.specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: never carry bearer authority in URLs or anywhere it can be logged; use sender-constrained tokens (DPoP/mTLS/HTTP message signatures) for capabilities, plus Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and log redaction. Test: crawl all responses/logs from an e2e run for any token-shaped string in URL, Referer or access log (must be zero).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Not evidence that capabilities-as-tokens fail; only that URL transport is a bad bearer channel.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Macaroon/Biscuit-style attenuable tokens are the survivor of the idea.

nodes.title: Caja (rewriting sanitizer) was archived after repeated bypasses; the freeze-the-realm descendant (SES/Hardened JS/Endo) survived in production
nodes.summary: Caja advisories: 2009 DOM-wrapper full-page escape and iframe schema hole, 2013 ES5 freezing and javascript: URI flaws, 2018-era XSS and Unicode-escape bypass found by a bounty hunter while Google Sites ran an unpatched Caja; Google archived repo 2021-01-31 citing unmaintained against modern research and known vulns (repo last push 2020-12-02). SES 'starts where Caja left off': lockdown() freezes intrinsics, compartments, harden(); third-party assessment June 2021 and July 2021 bug hunt found no criticals; Agoric kernel model formally verified sound. TC39: SES Stage 1 'very stale' (2022), recast as Hardened JavaScript; ShadowRealm orthogonal; Compartments cut to module loader API; Moddable XS implements. Endo: 1069 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-10-15; users Agoric, MetaMask (LavaMoat, Snaps run iframe+LavaMoat+SES layers). Documented non-guarantees: no CPU/memory/availability isolation (one agent), stack observable on JSC, covert channels via host endowments, TCB includes engine.
nodes.specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: in-process language-level capability sandboxes give authority control but NOT resource control; for untrusted/agent code AEGIS needs a resource-metered boundary (process/microVM/wasm with fuel) UNDER any language-level capability layer. Falsifiable: guest running `while(1)` or allocating unboundedly must be killed within X ms without affecting neighbours; SES alone fails this test by documented design.
nodes.overclaim_risk: TC39 thread is July 2022; status may have moved. No quantified lockdown overhead found.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Underclaim: Hardened JS is the only 'ocap web' lineage with real production users (MetaMask).

nodes.title: OCapN/CapTP: 30 years from E to a still 'pre-specification' protocol; interop only now being demonstrated
nodes.summary: ocapn/ocapn README: 'still pre-specification', may emerge from unifying Agoric (endo), Spritely Goblins and Cap'n Proto implementations; 254 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-10-13; AI-generated contributions to test suite barred. July 2026 IRC log: an independent implementation passed the conformance suite and was validating interop with Goblins (Unix, websockets, wasm message-port netlayers).
nodes.specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: do not put OCapN/CapTP on the critical path or as a wire dependency; adopt its object-capability semantics (sturdyrefs, third-party handoff, promise pipelining) as design vocabulary only. Reversal condition: published IETF-style spec with >=3 interoperating implementations and an external security review.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Spritely Goblins repo status not verified (codeberg, GitHub path 404).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Interop conformance suite existence is a positive maturity signal.

nodes.title: IronFleet/Ironclad proof cost (3.7 person-years, 5-8:1 proof:code) vs LLM proof synthesis: effort blocker partly removed, spec-fidelity blocker not
nodes.summary: IronFleet (SOSP'15): IronRSL+IronKV in 3.7 person-years total; proof:code ratio safety ~5:1, liveness ~8:1 (secondary lecture deck, conflicting summaries); Ironclad 5:1, EverCrypt F* 3:1 (arXiv 2405.01787 citing). LLM side: AutoVerus (arXiv 2409.13082) >90% of 150 Verus tasks, half under 30 s or 3 calls; vericoding benchmark (arXiv 2509.22908, Sep 2025; 12,504 specs: 3,029 Dafny, 2,334 Verus, 7,141 Lean) off-the-shelf success 82% Dafny, 44% Verus, 27% Lean; Dafny verification 68% (Jun 2024) -> 89% Opus-4.1, 96% union; AlgoVeri (2026) same tasks Dafny 40.3, Verus 24.7, Lean 7.8 (Gemini-3-Flash) - harness-sensitive.
nodes.specifics: No verified end-to-end HTTP server found (seL4 Microkit Rust HTTP server exists, unverified; kernel and libmicrokit verified). DESIGN IMPLICATION: verify small, high-leverage cores (parsers, token/policy evaluator, budget accounting) with Verus/Dafny where LLM synthesis is strongest, keep proofs agent-maintained; gate = proof must re-check in CI from scratch and each spec reviewed by a human-readable oracle (executable spec + differential test), because LLMs write easy-to-satisfy specs. Falsifiable: agent verification success on our own 20 core functions >=70% within 10 iterations else drop to property-test rung.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Benchmarks are toy-to-medium functions, not server-scale proofs; vericoding numbers are model/harness-dependent.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Dafny 82%/96% shows the 'proof is too costly' prior is out of date for small modules.

nodes.title: Evidence that LLMs do better with types and verifiers, but low-resource typed languages (OCaml, Racket, Ur/Web-class) lag
nodes.summary: Type-constrained decoding (ICLR/PLDI'25, arXiv 2504.09246, TypeScript): >50% fewer compile errors, +3.5-5.5% relative functional correctness, +37% relative repair. MultiPL-T (arXiv 2308.09895): OCaml/Racket fine-tuned models roughly double MultiPL-E; shows corpus-size gap. No head-to-head OCaml/Haskell/Rust agent study found. Strict-type feedback loops help; niche languages hurt via training scarcity.
nodes.specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: choose handler/SDK language by (agent pass@k with compiler feedback) not type-system purity; falsifiable protocol: same 30 handler tasks in Rust, OCaml, Gleam/Haskell with identical agent + compile loop, measure pass rate and iterations; adopt strongly-typed only if gap <10 points.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Evidence is on TypeScript and 2023-era open models, not 2026 frontier agents.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Frontier-agent proficiency in OCaml/Haskell may have largely closed; unmeasured.

nodes.title: seL4-based web stacks: verified kernel and Microkit, but no verified HTTP server found
nodes.summary: seL4 Foundation lists a Rust HTTP server on Microkit and a reference webserver; DornerWorks CAmkES web server isolates components on seL4; libmicrokit functional correctness proof reported (UNSW draft 2023-12). None carries app-level proofs. seL4 repo active (5.8k stars, pushed 2026-10-24).
nodes.specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: TCB ledger must say 'verified substrate, unverified server' for any seL4-hosted deployment; do not claim end-to-end proof; seL4 is an optional isolation backend, not a requirement.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Absence of evidence in a few searches, not exhaustive.
nodes.underclaim_risk: seL4 substrate proof is real and deployed.

nodes.title: Ocsigen/Eliom: typed full-stack OCaml framework alive 20 years with small community; no retrospective found
nodes.summary: Eliom (329 stars, pushed 2026-10-20) and ocsigenserver (104 stars, pushed 2026-10-20) remain actively maintained; claims static checking of valid HTML and no broken links. Experience report (HAL hal-00495903) blocked by Anubis; no HN/maintainer retrospective located.
nodes.specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: small-but-persistent typed stacks show maintenance can survive with institutional backing; but not a signal of agent suitability. Seed: fetch the experience report manually.

nodes.title: TechEmpower Framework Benchmarks sunset 2026-03-24 (repo archived): the canonical cross-framework comparison no longer updates
nodes.summary: Issue #10932 'Sunsetting the TechEmpower Framework Benchmarks': >20 rounds since 2013, repository archived read-only 2026-03-24. Historic Ur/Web and Hails comparisons cannot be re-run on current rounds; frameworks/OCaml still lists dream, httpaf, opium, webmachine; frameworks/Ur lists urweb.
nodes.specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: BENCH_PLAN must ship its own reproducible harness (pinned hardware spec, wrk2/oha, fortunes-like workload) rather than cite TFB; falsifiable: harness reproduces within 5% across 3 runs on the same box.
nodes.overclaim_risk: None significant; fact is verified from the issue body.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Archived repo can still be forked; community successors may exist (unchecked).

nodes.title: Why type-safe/capability/IFC web systems failed to be adopted: blocker matrix and which blockers coding agents remove
nodes.summary: Blockers across Ur/Web, Hails, Swift, Joe-E, Caja, E/Waterken, Fable: (1) annotation/proof burden - agents remove (Storm 1/19 LOC; vericoding 82% Dafny); (2) runtime overhead - mostly not the killer (LWeb 2-21%, Storm 0, Hails 1.7x vs Jetty); (3) library/stdlib taming and ecosystem (Joe-E, Ur/Web FFI, SES jQuery incompat) - NOT removed, agents can write but not make third-party code capability-safe; (4) bus factor/maintenance (Ur/Web 86% one author; Hails dormant 2016; Caja archived) - NOT removed; (5) confusing whole-program errors - partly removed (agents read errors); (6) policy-spec fidelity (Hails leaked posts) - NOT removed; (7) availability/resource control absent (SES) - needs OS/VM layer.
nodes.specifics: DESIGN IMPLICATION: invest agent effort in (1),(2),(5); invest human/process effort in (3),(4),(6); falsifiable roadmap check: every dependency on the critical path has >=2 maintainers org-level, a vendored reproducible build, and an executable-spec oracle.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Synthesis across papers; causality of 'died' is inferred, no authors' retrospective found for most.
nodes.underclaim_risk: May understate that these systems simply never had a funded product team.
